cohort: 7033 women who gave birth between January 1st, 2020, and January 1st, 2022, categorized into adolescent (19 years or younger) and adult groups.
finding: While adolescent pregnancy was associated with a higher risk of LBW, IUGR, and meconium fluid before adjusting for confounding factors, no statistically significant differences were found after adjustment, and adolescents had a lower risk of Cesarean section and gestational diabetes compared to adults.
mod_finding: Adolescents had a significantly lower risk of CS compared with adults.
birth_weight: Low birth weight (LBW) was more common in adolescent pregnancies before adjusting for confounding factors.
